project: Split Factory Sessions Fake-Service Runtime Tests into Focused Files
description: Mechanically reorganize the two giant Factory Sessions execution test files into behavior-focused package-local files so maintainers and queued BTRC/WSE lanes can understand and extend coverage with less context, while preserving every test, assertion, runtime outcome, and coverage value exactly.

context.customerAsk: Land a move-only split of fake_service_runtime_test.go and fake_service_test.go before queued WSE lanes begin changing the package. Keep the tests in the same package, group them by observed behavior, centralize shared test helpers without duplication, preserve the identical test inventory and coverage, and keep every resulting file at or below approximately 1,200 lines.
context.problem: The package's two largest test files contain more than 6,500 lines spanning unrelated execution behaviors. They consume maintainer and agent context, slow comprehension, increase bad-edit risk, and will create avoidable churn in the in-flight BTRC/WSE program.
context.solution: Capture an authoritative test-list and coverage baseline, then move whole tests and unchanged helpers into focused construction/start/lifecycle/read, replay/dispatch, runtime start/result/persistence, and runtime control/checkpoint/event/recording files within the existing execution package. Rebase and redo the moves over authoritative main if a concurrent WSE change lands, without changing product code or test behavior.

acceptanceCriteria: Existing tests are grouped into focused behavior files, shared test helpers have one package-local owner, and no resulting hand-maintained Go file in the package exceeds 1,200 lines.

Before-and-after output from go test -list '.*' ./pkg/services/factory_sessions/internal/execution/... contains no added, removed, or renamed test or example entry, with the comparison included as PR evidence.
go test ./pkg/services/factory_sessions/internal/execution/... passes with no test, subtest, assertion, fixture outcome, or observable runtime behavior changed.
Package coverage is captured with identical commands and options before and after, the reported value is unchanged, and both results are included as PR evidence.
The diff is dominated by mechanical moves and contains no production-code refactor, public-contract change, generated-file edit, assertion change, test addition/removal, or unrelated cleanup.
Typecheck and tests pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts are resolved against current main, and the PR is actually merged.
